subject: Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571
prompt: Sixteen survivors of the 1972 Andes plane crash were finally rescued after how long in the mountains?
why: The Fairchild crashed on 13 October 1972 and the last survivors were brought out on 23 December -- 72 days later, after two of them walked out over the mountains for help.

subject: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
prompt: Only one of the seven wonders of the ancient world is still standing today. Which?
why: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the oldest wonder on the list and the only one that survives; the other six were destroyed by earthquake, fire or war.

subject: Aurora
prompt: An aurora glows when charged particles from the Sun collide with which two gases high in Earth's atmosphere?
why: The collisions excite oxygen and nitrogen atoms, which release the energy as light -- oxygen gives the familiar green and red, nitrogen the blues and purples.

subject: At sign
prompt: Long before email, the @ symbol was an accounting and invoicing shorthand meaning what?
why: It meant 'at a rate of' -- as in '7 widgets @ 2 pounds per widget'. That commercial use is why it sat on typewriter keyboards decades before anyone put it in an email address.

subject: Neptune
prompt: Roughly how many Earth years does Neptune take to complete one orbit of the Sun?
why: Neptune orbits once every 164.8 years at about 30 astronomical units. It has completed only one full orbit since its discovery in 1846.

subject: Biggest ball of twine
prompt: The world's largest ball of twine by circumference is a roadside attraction in Cawker City -- in which US state?
why: The Cawker City, Kansas ball measured about 8 feet across and nearly 11 feet tall as of 2014. Several US towns claim a 'biggest ball of twine' record on different measures.

subject: Iron Dome
prompt: Israel's Iron Dome is built to intercept short-range rockets launched from up to roughly what distance away?
why: The system targets rockets and artillery shells fired from 4 to 70 kilometres away whose trajectory would carry them into a populated area.

subject: Sinking of the Titanic
prompt: How long did the Titanic stay afloat after striking the iceberg?
why: She struck at 23:40 on 14 April 1912 and sank at 02:20 on 15 April -- two hours and forty minutes, with lifeboat places for only about half those aboard.

subject: 27 Club
prompt: The 27 Club took hold after four rock stars died at that age between 1969 and 1971: Jimi Hendrix, Janis Joplin, Jim Morrison and who else?
why: Rolling Stones founder Brian Jones died in July 1969, weeks before Hendrix. Research has since found no real spike in musician deaths at 27 -- the cluster was coincidence.

subject: Magnus Carlsen
prompt: Magnus Carlsen holds the highest chess rating ever achieved. What was his peak?
why: Carlsen reached 2882 in 2014, passing Garry Kasparov's long-standing 2851. He has held the world number one ranking continuously since July 2011.

subject: Elizabeth Holmes
prompt: Theranos claimed its machines could run a huge range of blood tests from a sample as small as what?
why: The fingerprick claim drove a 9 billion dollar valuation and made Holmes, on paper, the youngest self-made female billionaire in the US. The technology did not work, and she was convicted of fraud.

subject: NATO phonetic alphabet
prompt: Alfa, Bravo, Charlie -- the spelling alphabet everyone calls the NATO phonetic alphabet was actually defined in the 1950s by which body?
why: Its official name is the International Radiotelephony Spelling Alphabet, defined in 1955-56 by the International Civil Aviation Organization for radio use where ordinary letter names are easily misheard.

subject: Prometheus
prompt: Zeus punished Prometheus for giving fire to humanity by chaining him to a rock where an eagle ate what, every day?
why: The liver regrew each night so the punishment could repeat forever -- the Greeks had noticed that the liver, alone among organs, regenerates.

subject: Camino de Santiago
prompt: The Camino de Santiago pilgrim routes all end at a cathedral in Galicia said to hold the remains of which apostle?
why: Santiago is Spanish for Saint James. Tradition places his tomb at Santiago de Compostela, and the network of walking routes to it has drawn pilgrims for over a thousand years.

subject: Go (game)
prompt: Which board game, invented in China more than 2,500 years ago, is believed to be the oldest one still played today?
why: Players place black and white stones to fence off territory. Over 20 million people play, most of them in East Asia.
